slot.archetype: Hess's law bond-energy calc combined with ΔH = ΔU + ΔnRT
slot.brief: Give a multi-step reaction cycle with a gaseous combustion step; ask for ΔU of the overall process using bond enthalpies plus the ΔH–ΔU conversion — hard bookkeeping.

stem: At $300\ \text{K}$, find $\Delta U$ for $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g)+\text{H}_2(g)\rightarrow\text{C}_2\text{H}_6(g)$. All combustion products contain $\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$. Use mean bond enthalpies $\text{C}={\text{C}}:614$, $\text{C}—\text{H}:413$, $\text{O}={\text{O}}:498$, $\text{C}={\text{O}}$ in $\text{CO}_2:799$, and $\text{O}—\text{H}:463\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; also, $\text{H}_2+\dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\rightarrow\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$ has $\Delta H=-242\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6+\dfrac{7}{2}\text{O}_2\rightarrow2\text{CO}_2+3\text{H}_2\text{O}(g)$ has $\Delta H=-1410\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Take $R=8.0\ \text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: For C₂H₄ combustion, bond enthalpies give ΔH = (614 + 4×413 + 3×498) − (4×799 + 4×463) = −1288 kJ mol⁻¹. Hess’s law: ΔH(hydrogenation) = −1288 − 242 − (−1410) = −120 kJ mol⁻¹. With Δn_g = −1, ΔU = ΔH − Δn_gRT = −120 + 2.4 = −117.6 kJ mol⁻¹.

working:
$\Delta H_{c}(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4)=[614+4(413)+3(498)]-[4(799)+4(463)]=-1288\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\Delta H_{\text{target}}=-1288-242+1410=-120\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. $\Delta n_g=1-2=-1$; $\Delta U=\Delta H-\Delta n_gRT=-120+\dfrac{8(300)}{1000}=-117.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Independent check: For C₂H₄ combustion, bond enthalpies give ΔH = (614 + 4×413 + 3×498) − (4×799 + 4×463) = −1288 kJ mol⁻¹. Hess’s law: ΔH(hydrogenation) = −1288 − 242 − (−1410) = −120 kJ mol⁻¹. With Δn_g = −1, ΔU = ΔH − Δn_gRT = −120 + 2.4 = −117.6 kJ mol⁻¹.
solution:
For combustion of ethene, using bond enthalpies, $\Delta H_c=[614+4(413)+3(498)]-[4(799)+4(463)]=-1288\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
By Hess’s law, $\Delta H_{\text{reaction}}=-1288-242+1410=-120\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
Here $\Delta n_g=1-2=-1$, so $\Delta U=\Delta H-\Delta n_gRT=-120+\frac{8(300)}{1000}=-117.6\ \text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
